summary.text: Jibreel Jalloh is a Brooklyn-born community organizer and nonprofit leader running for Assembly District 59 on the Working Families Party line after losing the June 2026 Democratic primary to incumbent Jaime Williams. According to his campaign website, he is an Obama Scholar who has also built a small business, and he is running on lowering costs, protecting homeowners, preventing gun violence, and addressing flooding.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, Jalloh is the son of a union nurse and a taxi driver who immigrated to New York, and he was born and raised in Brooklyn.
His campaign describes him as an Obama Scholar, community organizer, and nonprofit CEO.

According to his campaign, he helped stop a pesticide facility from being built near homes and schools, helped secure $1.6 million in funding to prevent gun violence, and supported workers in winning a union.
His campaign says he built a small business, giving him experience meeting payroll and dealing with government red tape.

In 2026 he ran in the Democratic primary for Assembly District 59 and lost to Jaime Williams, 33.8% to 66.0%; he advanced from the Working Families Party primary, which was canceled, and is on the November ballot on that line.
